$comment: One spec for which Python the research engine may run on. Read by three thin
bindings so they can never drift: bin/lib/resolve-python.mjs (the authority,
native Node so Windows works without bash), scripts/lib/resolve_python.sh
(sourced by run.sh and verify-research.sh), and hooks/_python.py.
MIN_PYTHON = (3,12), checked before the lib import.
There is NO upper bound: the comparison is `>=` only, so 3.14/3.15/4.x all pass
the gate untested. Hence `untestedAbove`: probe 3.13/3.12 first and warn, never
fail, above the tested ceiling — a future break should be diagnosable rather
Stock macOS ships 3.9, so 'no suitable Python' is the COMMON case, not the edge.

install.linux: sudo apt install python3.13   (or: pyenv install 3.13)

$comment_no_autoinstall: Never `curl | sh` the uv installer. hooks/pre_tool_use_policy.py already flags
that pattern, and installing an interpreter because someone enabled a marketing
plugin is the same overreach session_start.py documents having backed out of.
